pull.title: test: fix intermittent failure in p2p_tx_download.py
pull.body: Because `nodes[1]` time was not mocked in test_block_inv, it was possible for wall clock to advance 2s by the time `nodes[0]` had delivered a tx announcement to it. Then, `nodes[1]` would request the tx from a test peer, never receive the tx, and fail in sync_mempools().

events.message:
test: fix intermittent failure in p2p_tx_download.py

Because nodes[1] time was not mocked in test_block_inv, it was
possible for wall clock to advance 2s by the time nodes[0] had
delivered a tx announcement to it. Then, nodes[1] would request
the tx from a test peer, never receive the tx, and fail in
sync_mempools().

A summary of reviews will appear here.

It's possible to simulate `nodes[1]` not running with the following diff on 8130b3b8836879915e82730eb818ee6b58c28168:

```diff
diff --git a/test/functional/p2p_tx_download.py b/test/functional/p2p_tx_download.py
index aa43cc18e2..4a83e44b91 100755
--- a/test/functional/p2p_tx_download.py
+++ b/test/functional/p2p_tx_download.py
@@ -116,6 +116,8 @@ class TxDownloadTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         self.log.info("Put the tx in node 0's mempool")
         self.nodes[0].sendrawtransaction(tx['hex'])
 
+        time.sleep(2)
+
         # Since node 1 is connected outbound to an honest peer (node 0), it
         # should get the tx within a timeout.
         # However, node 0 sees the same connection as inbound, so it may not
```

I tested the master and PR versions using the same binary and Crypt-iQ's reproducer, adding a delay after `sendrawtransaction`.

On master, with a 2-second delay, 2/5 runs failed due to mempool sync timeouts. With the PR, both runs passed. Increasing the delay to 5 seconds made master pass, but runs took around 83 seconds instead of 26, while the PR remained around 26 seconds.

Looking at node1's debug log, master requests the wtx from peer 4, which never responds, and retries node0 only after 60 seconds. With the PR, it requests from peer 0 almost immediately after receiving the inventory. So this isn't just fixing a flaky test; it also avoids a silent 60-second slowdown when the race occurs.

comments.body: you can remove both, the outer loop already takes care of this.

I think if you select `        self.nodes[1].setmocktime(now)` the test will break, because `NONPREF_PEER_TX_DELAY` can never hit? Sure, it never hit in practise before either, but it seems a bit odd for the test to imply it can be hit when now it can deterministically never hit. 

Also, what does "races" refer to when both nodes use mocktime? The patch here doesn't seem right, or at least incomplete.

I think the issue you are seeing was introduced in 2706c5b7c8 (I haven't tried this).

So the possible fixes are:

* Revert 2706c5b7c8 (and go back to rough "best-effort" test coverage)
* Properly use mocktime to keep the test coverage (and ideally exercise the exact code triggers mentioned here)

I should have spent a bit more time before opening the PR. I do think there's a flake here though.

I think currently the test is broken on master:
- `self.nodes[0]` uses mocktime and `self.nodes[1]` does not. So when `self.nodes[0].bumpmocktime(timeout)` is used, it doesn't make much sense because that timeout is actually meant for `self.nodes[1]` since it doesn't have the tx and may request the tx from the test peers and then fallback to requesting it from `self.nodes[0]`. I think `self.nodes[0]` mocktime does need to be bumped, but only around the order of `INBOUND_INVENTORY_BROADCAST_INTERVAL` so it can actually announce to `self.nodes[1]`.
- the second thing is that because `self.nodes[1]` does not use mock time, its real clock can advance before `self.nodes[0]` sends the inv. If time advances on `self.nodes[1]` by `NONPREF_PEER_TX_DELAY` before `self.nodes[0]` can announce, `self.nodes[1]` will request from a test peer first. It will expire after ~60s (`GETDATA_TX_INTERVAL`) and while this is happening, the `sync_mempools` timeout of 60s may be hit.

Is this too much of an edge case?
